audit.whatIsWrong: Levels 1, 4-5 and 6 rendered as Skill while their whys describe Quinn winning each; 2+ items rendered as Quinn while whys[6], spikes[3] and the late paragraph all say Swain outscales.
audit.why: Packet levelChart is [Quinn x6, Skill] and Quinn wins 56.92% over 260 games. whys[0] 'Swain is a weak level-1', whys[3] 'You out-trade a Swain who hasn't stacked souls' and whys[4] 'use your own R to roam' are all Quinn-sided.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 3 and 4 to Quinn; row 6 to Swain — all four proposed as one atomic group across both layers, with phases[6].why rewritten so the row and its reason agree.

audit.why: Quinn levels 1-2, level 3 with the full pattern, first-item lethality, Swain at 2+ items with soul stacks — correct and ordered. Demonic Ascension's 120s flat cooldown and Nevermove's 12s now appear so the windows are countable.
audit.corrected: Numbers written into breakdown.cooldowns and whys[2].

audit.whatIsWrong: Two errors repeated across the page. First, the ROOT is credited to W ('W bomb and root', 'before he can W root') — Nevermove (E) is the root and pull; Vision of Empire (W) is a delayed eye that damages, slows and reveals, and roots nothing. Second, whys[2], spikes[1], early and mid all tell the player to 'blind his Q' — Death's Hand is an ability and a blind does not touch it. Also unstated: Nevermove roots on its RETURN wave, and it cancels Behind Enemy Lines.
audit.why: Riot text for Nevermove: 'Swain launches a wave of demonic power forward. It then returns to Swain and roots enemies it hits.' Riot text for Vision of Empire: 'opens a demon eye that deals damage and slows enemies.' Quinn's Q hinders vision, which only causes basic attacks to miss. Quinn's R carries the channel flag and the missing-interactions file flags Nevermove as the cancel.
audit.corrected: Root reattributed to Nevermove, the return-wave timing stated (it is the actual dodging skill in this lane), the blind claim removed from whys[2] and wants.foe[0], and the channel cancel recorded.

audit.whatIsWrong: Demonic Ascension was named the tracked cooldown and the advice was 'poke when it's down' — but the form has no fixed duration, so 'down' is not a state the player can read off a timer.
audit.why: Riot text: 'This form is indefinite as long as Swain drains enemy champions.' Nevermove at 12s is the cooldown that actually gates his kill threat.
audit.corrected: Nevermove named the matchup cooldown; the indefinite-drain rule stated in dosFull[0].d so the player stops waiting for it to expire.

audit.why: report[8].t already builds early anti-heal, which the missing-interactions file confirms is required — Ravenous Flock heals him and permanently raises his max health off Soul Fragments, and it also means stacking raw resistances is the wrong answer.
